paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is really about. Joseph is locked up, and he's STILL looking at the two men beside him and asking, "Why are your faces so downcast today?" (Genesis 40:7). Then he says, "Don't interpretations belong to God?" (Genesis 40:8). He doesn't take the credit, and what he says comes true on the third day (Genesis 40:20-22).

Now look at what Joseph asks for. He tells the cupbearer, "please remember me and show me kindness by mentioning me to Pharaoh" (Genesis 40:14). And then comes the line that stings: the cupbearer "did not remember Joseph; he forgot all about him" (Genesis 40:23). I think that one hurts, because Joseph did his part and nothing came back.

So what do you do with that, baker? Maybe you've done right by somebody and they never called you back. I've sat in the back of a junk drawer for years, so I know that feeling. This passage doesn't tell you the wait means nothing. It shows a man who keeps caring for people and keeps pointing to God, even while he's stuck, and the story isn't over.
